newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia troops to leave Chechnya next week - agencies.
newsitem.headline: Russia troops to leave Chechnya next week - agencies.

text.p: Russia plans to complete its troop withdrawal from Chechnya by January 5, meeting the terms of a peace deal struck with separatist rebels, Russian news agencies quoted officials as saying on Monday.

Itar-Tass quoted chief of staff of the Interior Ministry forces, Pavel Maslov, as saying some 8,000 servicemen under the ministry's command are still to leave Chechnya to meet the self-imposed deadline.

Interfax quoted sources in the armed forces' general staff as saying its troops are also to leave Chechnya by January 5. The source said there are altogether 400 servicemen of the armed forces remaining in Chechnya.
Russia's military command in Chechnya has said it would pull out its last combat unit from Chechnya by Monday, leaving only logistics and transport units behind.
But the general staff source quoted by Interfax mentioned some combat units of the 205 Motor Rifle Brigade as still remaining in the southern region.
Under the peace deal signed on August 31, Moscow promised to withdraw its forces, which were sent to Chechnya in December 1994 to quell the region's independence bid.
Tens of thousands of people have died in 21 months of the ill-fated war in which Russian troops have suffered many humiliating defeats .
The rebels, for their part, agreed to postpone by five years a decision on Chechnya's political status. But their leaders make little secret that they still want full independence.

Under their pressure President Boris Yeltsin earlier this month abandoned the idea of keeping the 205th brigade and another brigade of Interior Ministry forces permanently in Chechnya and ordered a complete withdrawal.
The separatist leadership has called local elections for January 27 to elect a Chechen president and parliament.
They have been pressing Moscow to complete the pullout by that date.

Five candidates -- separatist leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev, premier Aslan Maskhadov, prominent field commander Shamil Basayev, security supremo Akhmed Zakayev and propaganda chief Movladi Udugov, have so far provided the electoral commission with 10,000 signatures of support.
The five, known as "resistance candidates," have failed in their attempts to rally behind a single candidate but have vowed to stick together after the polls.
